For this benchmark, retain each user’s binary hit@10 and compare configurations on identical users and candidate sets. Apply a paired bootstrap, resampling users within each category while preserving outcomes across configurations; recompute the equally weighted four-category mean difference and its 95% interval. Report category differences and discordant wins/losses; McNemar’s test addresses paired binary outcomes. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted models and fixed candidates, not training-seed variability or negative-sampling variability. See [paired bootstrap documentation](https://cache-docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) and [NIST’s McNemar reference](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman1/auxillar/mcnemar.htm).

Repeatedly selecting the best validation result produces optimistic estimates, even with a fixed training seed. Predeclare a small comparison family, practical improvement threshold, trial budget and stopping rule; record every attempted configuration and checkpoint selection. Holm correction can address multiplicity for prespecified valid tests, but does not repair unrestricted adaptive search. Treat selected validation gains as exploratory; use the host’s untouched final evaluation for confirmation without changing splits. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf) explain selection bias; [statsmodels](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/_modules/statsmodels/stats/multitest.html) implements Holm adjustment.

For attribution within the GPU budget, use a small full factorial: two binary changes require four configurations. Estimate interaction as HR11−HR10−HR01+HR00, with paired user-bootstrap intervals and category-specific contrasts. For more factors, fractional factorial screening saves runs but aliases effects; document aliases and reserve budget for resolving promising interactions. Cached hit vectors make uncertainty analysis inexpensive. Fixed seed 42 limits conclusions to that training realization; users cannot substitute for independent training replicates. [NIST](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pri/section3/pri3343.htm) explains factorial confounding.
